extra.message: User-controlled id from req.query.id (routes/users/user.js:28 and :205 via getUser) is concatenated directly into the SQL string "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id =" + parameter[0] + ";" and passed to pool.query(). This is an error-based SQL injection allowing an attacker to alter the query and extract or modify arbitrary data.

Login credentials (username/password) from the authentication form are concatenated unescaped into "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email ='" + parameter[0] + "' AND password = '" + parameter[1] + "'". An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication or dump the users table.

User-supplied username is concatenated into the LIKE clause: "select ... from users where username like '%" + username + "%';". Reachable via /blind-sqli, /xss-exercise, /second-order-sqli (stored username) and /xxe. This is a SQL injection (blind/second-order) allowing data exfiltration; the blacklist in utils/utility.js is bypassable.

The ip value from req.body.ip (routes/users/user.js:135) is concatenated into a shell command 'ping -c 3 ' + ip which is executed via child_process.exec() on line 66. Shell metacharacters (e.g. 127.0.0.1; id) allow arbitrary OS command execution.

The filename from req.query.filename (routes/users/user.js:144) is joined to __dirname and read with fs.readFile() on line 81. No canonicalization or validation is performed, so '../' sequences allow arbitrary file retrieval outside the intended directory (e.g. filename=../../../../etc/passwd).

User input from req.body.search (routes/users/user.js:156) is concatenated directly into a RegExp constructor: new RegExp('(public\\[\\d+\\] +.*' + search + '.*)'). This allows regex injection (matching unintended log lines / bypassing the intended filter) and catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) that can hang the server.

Attacker-controlled XML from req.body.search (routes/users/user.js:168) is parsed by libxml.parseXmlString() with the parser option noent:true (line 122) enabled, which resolves external entities. A crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY payload can read local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or perform SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The user-controlled cookie req.cookies.user (routes/users/user.js:177) is base64-decoded and passed to node-serialize's serialize.unserialize() on line 140. node-serialize executes serialized functions (the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ marker), so this is insecure deserialization leading to remote code execution.

In searchUserBlackList the raw user input is concatenated into HTML: htmlResponse = "

User " + username + " not present";. This response is rendered unescaped with <%- htmlResponse %> in views/reflected-xss.ejs:65. Because only the SQLi blacklist is checked (not XSS) and it is bypassable, an input such as is reflected and executed.

The user's fullname is stored unescaped at registration (models/usersModel.js:56) and rendered with the unescaped EJS tag <%- fullName %> (also at line 42 and views/navigation.ejs:17). A registered user can store an XSS payload in fullname/username that executes for every viewer, giving stored XSS.

The URL parameter 'default' is read via getUrlVars() (line 15) and written into the DOM with document.write("") without HTML encoding. A crafted ?default= executes script in the victim's browser (DOM-based XSS).

idorViewProfile looks up getUser(req.query.id) using an attacker-controlled id without verifying it belongs to the authenticated user (req.user.id). Any authenticated user can read any other user's profile details (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: idorUpdateProfile updates updateUserById(req.body, req.query.id) for an arbitrary id taken from the request, with no check that the id matches the session user. Any authenticated user can modify any other user's fullname, username, email and phone (IDOR / horizontal privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: changePassword uses req.body.id (a client-controlled hidden field) rather than the authenticated session user id. A logged-in user can submit an arbitrary id and reset any other account's password, resulting in account takeover.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is hardcoded as 'secrettobechanged'. Anyone with the source can forge or tamper with session cookies, undermining authentication. Secrets should be supplied via environment variables and be strong/random.

The session cookie is configured with httpOnly:false and secure:false. Without HttpOnly, any XSS can steal the session cookie, and without Secure it is transmitted over plain HTTP. This weakens session protection.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The session middleware uses saveUninitialized:true and resave:true, and the login flow (routes/users/user.js:13) calls req.logIn without regenerating the session id. An attacker who fixes a known session id can have the victim authenticate into it, resulting in session fixation.

User passwords are stored in plaintext: registerUser inserts user.password directly, and authenticateUser compares the plaintext password in SQL. A database compromise exposes all credentials; passwords should be salted and hashed (the existing utils/sha512.js helper is unused).
Database errors are returned verbatim to the client via res.send(err) (also at lines 213 and 172). This leaks SQL error messages, schema details and stack information that aid further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: State-changing POST endpoints (e.g. /change-password, /update-profile, /idor, /register) have no CSRF protection. Although csurf is listed in package.json it is never applied in app.js, so a malicious site can force an authenticated user's browser to submit these requests.
